key_finding: AAOI is structurally Thompson Lin's company. He founded it in 1997, has been Chairman/President/CEO since inception, and after 28+ years remains the dominant executive presence. The board around him includes a substantive laser/optics-industry veteran (Richard Black, ex-CEO ECRM the laser-imaging company sold to Kodak in 2021) and an Asia-semi industry insider (Che-Wei Lin, President of ASMedia and Corporate VP at ASUSTek). The composition reflects AAOI's actual operating profile — Sugar Land vertical integration plus Taiwan-China-US manufacturing — rather than the financial-engineering board that a near-IPO or pre-listing company would assemble. There is no separate COO. CFO Stefan Murry also serves as Chief Strategy Officer (dual role).

ceo_founder.framing: Lin is unusual in modern semi: a working scientist who became CEO of the company he founded out of his research lab and has stayed in the role for 28 years. The combination of nuclear-engineering background + electrical-engineering doctorate + decades of laser-component work is what built AAOI's vertically integrated structure. The Missouri ties (his graduate alma mater) recur in the board composition — Che-Wei Lin also has a Missouri MS in EE.

He has audit-committee-chair experience at GSI Group (a public optical/photonics company) and Alliance Fiber Optics Products. The institutional knowledge he brings to a laser-and-optics company audit is unmatched on this board. The Princeton IAS trustee role and the Texas A&M / Harvard MBA pedigree mark him as part of the senior US technology-business establishment.

board_composition_observation: The board is unusually substantive for a sub-$1B small-cap that operates in optical/photonics. Three directors — Black (laser imaging), Che-Wei Lin (Asia semi/chipsets), DeLaney (Shell trading/EE) — carry deep technical and operating experience in adjacent industries; Loboa brings academic rigor; Yeh brings community-banking and real-estate stability; Chen brings cross-border industrial experience. There is no separate financial-engineering board member of the kind Sivers assembled (no ex-Citi CFO, no ex-Deutsche Bank Head of Corporate Finance) — AAOI's board is built for OPERATIONAL governance of a vertically-integrated semi company, not for a pending US listing or transformative M&A. That difference matters. AAOI is run by a founder-CEO who is also chairman. The board is configured to advise and audit, not to drive strategic change.
